META_DESCRIPTION: Explore how regular investing and compound interest can grow over time.

SUMMARY_EMPTY: Enter your details to see your projection.
CHART_ARIA_SELECTED: Investment chart: portfolio value reaches {value} after {duration}.
CHART_ARIA_PROJECTION: The dashed lime line shows a possible {duration} projection.
CHART_PLACEHOLDER: Your investment timeline will appear here.
DID_YOU_KNOW_EMPTY: Giving your investments more time can give compound growth more room to work.
DID_YOU_KNOW_TEMPLATE: If you invest for {duration} more {unit}, your portfolio could be {percent}% larger, reaching {value}.
DID_YOU_KNOW_LIMIT: A future projection of at least 2 more months or years does not fit within the 100-year limit.
DID_YOU_KNOW_UNAVAILABLE: This future projection is beyond the calculator's numeric range.
HOW_INTRO: A monthly investing rhythm, with each deposit earning interest only after it is added.
HOW_STEP_ONE_COPY: The projection begins with a R$0.00 balance before the first contribution.
HOW_STEP_TWO_COPY: At the start of each month, the invested balance earns the monthly interest rate.
HOW_STEP_THREE_COPY: The monthly contribution is added after interest. The first deposit earns for all remaining months, and the final deposit earns no interest.
HOW_STEP_FOUR_COPY: An effective annual interest rate is converted to its equivalent monthly rate before compounding. A yearly income amount is split into twelve monthly contributions.
HOW_FORMULA: Monthly balance = previous balance × (1 + monthly rate) + monthly contribution
HOW_FOOTNOTE: Growth percentage compares estimated interest with total contributions. Estimates exclude taxes, fees, inflation, and changing returns.
EXAMPLE_INTRO: See one possible outcome using a steady contribution and an effective annual interest rate.
EXAMPLE_NOTE: The first monthly contribution earns for 119 months. The final contribution is added at the end and earns no interest.
EXAMPLE_USE_BUTTON: Use these values in the calculator
EXAMPLE_ERROR: The example could not be calculated right now.
FOOTER_NOTE: A simple way to picture the road ahead.
